# History - LangChain4J - System Message

This example demonstrates how the message history limits the number of messages
sent to the model. The system message plays a special role, as it is never
removed, while only the last $n$ user messages are retained in the history.

This example operates solely on the message history and does not interact with a
model.

```java
package demo;

import dev.langchain4j.data.message.SystemMessage;
import dev.langchain4j.data.message.UserMessage;
import dev.langchain4j.memory.chat.MessageWindowChatMemory;

public final class Main {

    public static void main(final String[] args) {
        final MessageWindowChatMemory chatMemory = MessageWindowChatMemory.builder()
                .maxMessages(10)
                .build();

        chatMemory.add(SystemMessage.systemMessage("The system message..."));

        for (int i = 1; i <= 15; i++) {
            chatMemory.add(UserMessage.from("User message " + i));
        }

        System.out.println("The history has " + chatMemory.messages().size() + " messages");
        chatMemory.messages()
                .forEach(m -> System.out.println(" - " + m + " (of type " + m.getClass().getSimpleName() + ")"));
    }

    private Main() {}
}
```

## Prerequisites

- [Oracle Java 25](https://www.oracle.com/java/technologies/downloads/#java25)

## Run the example

1. Build the application

   ```shell
   ./mvnw clean package
   ```

   (*Optional*) Verify that the application was created and the dependencies
   copied.

   ```shell
   tree --sort=name './target/libs'
   ```

   The application JAR file and its dependencies.

   ```
   ./target/libs
   ├── history-langchain4j-system-message-1.0.0.jar
   ├── jackson-annotations-2.21.jar
   ├── jackson-core-2.21.1.jar
   ├── jackson-databind-2.21.1.jar
   ├── jspecify-1.0.0.jar
   ├── langchain4j-1.13.1.jar
   ├── langchain4j-core-1.13.1.jar
   ├── logback-classic-1.5.32.jar
   ├── logback-core-1.5.32.jar
   ├── opennlp-tools-2.5.4.jar
   └── slf4j-api-2.0.17.jar

   1 directory, 11 files
   ```

2. Run the program

   ```shell
   java \
     --class-path './target/libs/*' \
     demo.Main
   ```

   Notice that the system message remains in the history, even though other user
   messages have been removed.

   ```
   The history has 10 messages
    - SystemMessage { text = "The system message..." } (of type SystemMessage)
    - UserMessage { name = null, contents = [TextContent { text = "User message 7" }], attributes = {} } (of type UserMessage)
    - UserMessage { name = null, contents = [TextContent { text = "User message 8" }], attributes = {} } (of type UserMessage)
    - UserMessage { name = null, contents = [TextContent { text = "User message 9" }], attributes = {} } (of type UserMessage)
    - UserMessage { name = null, contents = [TextContent { text = "User message 10" }], attributes = {} } (of type UserMessage)
    - UserMessage { name = null, contents = [TextContent { text = "User message 11" }], attributes = {} } (of type UserMessage)
    - UserMessage { name = null, contents = [TextContent { text = "User message 12" }], attributes = {} } (of type UserMessage)
    - UserMessage { name = null, contents = [TextContent { text = "User message 13" }], attributes = {} } (of type UserMessage)
    - UserMessage { name = null, contents = [TextContent { text = "User message 14" }], attributes = {} } (of type UserMessage)
    - UserMessage { name = null, contents = [TextContent { text = "User message 15" }], attributes = {} } (of type UserMessage)
   ```

   Please note that the history can contain only one system message. If a second
   system message is added, it will replace the first.
